Ophthalmic screening support

Provenance-aware ophthalmic screening

An empirical audit of a widely used fundus benchmark, and a human-in-the-loop screening prototype built around what it found.

What this project asks

Public four-class fundus benchmarks are widely reported at 95–96% accuracy. This asks how much of that is retinal pathology and how much is where the image came from, re-evaluates standard classifiers under a corrected protocol, and builds a human-in-the-loop screening prototype around the answer.

Findings

Acquisition provenance nearly determines the label

Majority baseline 26.0%. A four-row source lookup table reaches 69.1%. A metadata-only classifier reaches 66.7% without seeing a single pixel. Holding source constant removes the signal in odir_jpg512 (+0.004) but not in crop_jpg256 (+0.219) or png_highres (+0.284): provenance explains the diabetic-retinopathy and normal classes almost entirely, and contributes little to separating cataract from glaucoma. Both halves are reported.

Patient leakage is real, confirmed on a deployable model

A linear head gains +0.005 (p=0.75) — it cannot memorise. A fine-tuned ResNet50 on a GPU gains +0.022 at p<0.001; a 1-NN retriever gains +0.045 at p≈0. Splitting by patient matters more as model capacity rises.

The model does not transfer across acquisition sources

Trained on ODIR, it scores below majority-class guessing on three of four unseen sources.

It is not a demographics detector

Cataract-vs-rest AUROC holds near 0.94 under age and sex matching, and age plus sex alone score below the majority baseline.

Raw OCR confidence is near-useless for clinical field extraction

AUROC 0.52 and 0.64. A learned correctness estimator reaches 0.98 and 0.99; the signal is in value format and length, not in OCR confidence.

Two negative results are reported, not tuned away

The protocol ladder's initial null, later corrected by the capacity sweep; and the learned deferral gate, which lost to two hand-written rules and was dropped by a kill rule written before the run.

The prototype

The referral document never changes the diagnosis. That is enforced in code — predict_image() does not take the document as a parameter — and the interface mirrors it: the image pathway and the document pathway are separate columns that meet only at the decision banner. The referral, and how reliably it was read, decide only whether the system answers.

  • Worklist — the triage queue, deferred cases first
  • Case review — one case end to end, with the grounded assistant
  • Figures — all 14, regenerated from results/
  • Full results — generated from results/, nothing transcribed

Running it

The live app needs a server, because screening runs a PyTorch model:

  • pip install -r requirements.txt && pip install -e .
  • python scripts/serve.py → http://127.0.0.1:8000
  • python scripts/run_all.py rebuilds every experiment (~70 min, CPU)

The repository is self-contained: the committed model is 34 KB, and the ImageNet backbone is fetched from torchvision at runtime. ODIR images are not redistributed, so a fresh clone starts in upload-only mode.

Honest limits

  • 203 cataract and 182 glaucoma patients — intervals, not point estimates.
  • Every model sits on frozen ImageNet features; a fine-tuned backbone may differ.
  • The referral corpus is synthetic. Technical evaluation, never clinical validation.
  • Attribution shows where attribution falls, not that the model sees a lesion.
  • No prospective data, no clinical trial, no regulatory clearance.

what are the limitations?

Limitations: trained on a public research dataset with 203 cataract and 182 glaucoma patients; not validated on prospective clinical data; the referral documents used in development were synthetic. This is an academic screening prototype, not a medical device. It does not diagnose. A qualified clinician reviews every case and makes every decision.

Answers are assembled from this case's structured outputs only. The assistant cannot generate clinical text and refuses questions it has no field for.

Results

Every number here is read from results/ by scripts/summarise_results.py. Nothing is transcribed by hand.

Not a medical device. Synthetic documents are not clinical data. No clinical validation is claimed.

1. Dataset

ODIR-5K, four-class subset: 5058 images from 2910 patients.

classimagespatientsmulti-findingmean age
C29320331 (10.6%)66.8
D16081027223 (13.9%)55.7
G28418266 (23.2%)63.0
N2873185257 (2.0%)57.2
  • 2148 patients contribute both eyes - the mechanism behind patient-level leakage.
  • 354 patients carry different diagnoses in each eye, so grouping is by patient but stratification is at eye level.
  • 91 distinct resolutions, no EXIF: ODIR provenance cannot be labelled cleanly.

    • Confounds to report, not hide. Cataract patients average ~11 years older than diabetic-retinopathy patients; sex distribution differs by class; and 23.2% of glaucoma rows name a second condition in the annotation. ODIR is less confounded, not clean.

    2. Provenance audit (RQ1)

    The merged four-class benchmark is not one dataset. Acquisition source is assigned from file properties alone - never from the class folder - and it almost determines the label.

  • Majority-class baseline: 26.0%
  • Source lookup table alone: 69.1% (no model, no pixels)
    • experimentquestionbaselineprobelift
    E0aclass from file metadata only0.2600.667+0.407
    E0bsource from FOV-normalised pixels0.3980.749+0.351
    E0c-isource from geometry only0.3980.702+0.304
    E0c-ii[odir_jpg512]predict class from pixels within source=odir_jpg5120.6400.644+0.004
    E0c-ii[crop_jpg256]predict class from pixels within source=crop_jpg2560.5160.736+0.219
    E0c-ii[png_highres]predict class from pixels within source=png_highres0.4970.781+0.284

    The anti-circularity control (E0c-ii). Within a single acquisition source, provenance is constant, so anything a probe achieves must come from retinal content:

  • odir_jpg512 (n=1678): 0.640 -> 0.644, lift +0.004
  • crop_jpg256 (n=1240): 0.516 -> 0.736, lift +0.219
  • png_highres (n=201): 0.497 -> 0.781, lift +0.284

    • Every diabetic-retinopathy image is a .jpeg and no other class contains one, so file extension alone is a perfect DR detector on this benchmark. The cataract/glaucoma sources split roughly 50/50, so provenance explains the DR and normal classes almost entirely and contributes little to separating cataract from glaucoma. Both halves of that belong in the paper.

    3. Deduplication

    Detector: FOV-normalised 64x64 fingerprint, cosine similarity. Rejected alternative: ImageNet ResNet50 embedding cosine - see calibration table.

  • Ground truth: 1654 known duplicate pairs (a merged-benchmark image sharing a filename with an ODIR image), calibrated against the hardest available negatives.
  • Operating threshold 0.999: precision 0.9895, recall 0.9728.
  • Within ODIR: 2 duplicate groups, 2 images removed -> 5056 images, 2909 patients.
  • 1626 merged-benchmark images are ODIR copies and are therefore excluded from cross-source test data.

    • Caveat carried into the paper: recall is measured over ODIR<->merged ground-truth pairs; recall for within-ODIR duplicates is not directly measurable.

    A methods note worth publishing on its own: ImageNet-embedding cosine similarity fails as a duplicate detector on fundus images. At threshold 0.999 it recovers 0% of known duplicates, while the FOV-normalised fingerprint recovers 97%. Fundus images are visually homogeneous and the copies differ by a large downscale, which ImageNet features are not invariant to.

    4. Protocol ladder (RQ2)

    Model held fixed, only the split varies. Frozen ResNet50 features with a logistic head.

    rungnaccuracymacro-F195% CI
    image_level50580.59750.5496[0.5308, 0.5677]
    patient_disjoint50580.59510.5444[0.5248, 0.5622]
    patient_disjoint_dedup50560.59490.5476[0.5282, 0.5675]
    provenance_controlled15350.60980.5048[0.4735, 0.5383]
    comparisonmacro-F1 dropMcNemar p
    image_level -> patient_disjoint+0.00520.746733
    image_level -> patient_disjoint_dedup+0.00190.750243
    image_level -> provenance_controlled+0.04470.143081

    Result on frozen features: H2 is falsified as run. No rung differs significantly from any other; all confidence intervals overlap.

    This was a lower bound, and E3 (below) closes it. A frozen linear head has almost no capacity to memorise, and leakage inflates a score by letting a model recall a near-copy it has already seen. A fine-tuned backbone can memorise - and does.

    4a. Fine-tuned confirmation (E3)

    E1 (frozen features) found no significant leakage inflation, with the caveat that a linear head cannot memorise. E1b showed inflation rises with the capacity to memorise, using frozen-feature models up to a 1-NN retriever. This closes the loop with the model people actually deploy: a resnet50, fine-tuned end-to-end (colab/train_models.ipynb, 8 epochs, seed 42, 384px).

    rungnmacro-F195% CI
    image-level (leaky)50580.6797[0.6611, 0.6967]
    patient-disjoint + dedup50560.6579[0.6393, 0.6768]

    Inflation: +0.0218 macro-F1 (McNemar p = 0.0006825, 886 discordant pairs out of 5056 paired predictions).

    modelcapacity to memoriseinflationMcNemar p
    logistic head (E1)none+0.00520.75
    fine-tuned resnet50 (E3)realistic+0.02180.0006825
    1-NN retriever (E1b)pure+0.0453~0

    Monotonic in capacity, and significant for the model people would actually deploy. This confirms E1b rather than merely being consistent with it: E1's null was a genuine artefact of using a low-capacity head, not a property of the dataset. The finding is no longer "a 1-NN toy model shows leakage" - it is "a deployable fine-tuned CNN shows leakage, at p < 0.001."

    Caveat carried forward: one seed, one backbone, 8 epochs. E13's seed-stability and Holm-Bonferroni correction were run on the frozen-feature models only; the fine-tuned result should be read as confirmatory rather than as independently seed-tested.

    4b. Does inflation depend on memorisation? (E1b)

    E1's null invites an obvious objection: a frozen linear head cannot memorise, and leakage is exploited by memorisation. So rather than reaching for a GPU, sweep the variable that actually matters - capacity - holding features and splits fixed. 1-NN is a pure retriever: if a patient's fellow eye is in the training set, it will find it.

    modelimage-levelpatient-disjointinflationMcNemar p
    logistic0.54960.5444+0.00520.746733
    mlp0.58430.5569+0.02740.200594
    knn_50.52500.5044+0.02070.000646
    knn_10.55760.5124+0.04530.0

    Verdict: inflation grows with memorisation capacity - E1's null was an artefact of using a low-capacity head.

    This corrects E1. Patient leakage on this dataset is real and is exploitable - by models that memorise. A pure retriever gains +0.045 macro-F1 from ignoring patient identity, at p ~ 0. The parametric models show smaller, non-significant gains. The practical implication for anyone using this benchmark is that patient-disjoint splitting matters more as model capacity rises, which is precisely the direction the field is moving.

    4c. Transfer to unseen acquisition sources (E5)

    Trained on 5056 ODIR images; tested on merged-benchmark images after removing 1626 confirmed ODIR copies, so nothing in the test set was seen in training.

    sourcenclassesmajority-class accmodel accmacro-F1
    crop_jpg2561223C,G0.5170.3300.228
    eyepacs_jpeg1098D1.0000.2970.115
    odir_jpg51269C,G,N0.4490.5070.412
    png_highres201C,G0.5020.1040.093

    The model does not transfer. On three of four sources it scores below the accuracy of always guessing that source's majority class. Each source is class-restricted - itself a symptom of the provenance confound - so results are reported per source and never pooled.

    Two caveats. The in-domain model is itself weak (macro-F1 0.55 on frozen features), so poor transfer is partly a weak model rather than purely a domain gap. And this measures transfer under a documented change of acquisition source, not generalisation in the unqualified sense.

    4d. Is it a disease detector or a demographics detector? (E11)

    ODIR is less confounded, not clean: cataract patients average 11 years older than diabetic-retinopathy patients, and the sex distribution differs by class. Networks read age and sex from fundus photographs accurately, so this is testable rather than merely a limitations-section caveat.

    Demographics alone, no image: accuracy 0.5560 against a 0.5678 majority baseline (lift -0.0119), macro-F1 0.2531. Age and sex carry no usable class signal here - the classifier does worse than always guessing the majority class.

    conditionnpatientsmacro-F195% CIcataract AUROC
    unrestricted505629090.5476[0.5283, 0.5668]0.9462
    age_matched9647790.5385[0.5030, 0.5718]0.9414
    sex_matched9727920.5302[0.4999, 0.5619]0.9406
    multi_finding_removed467927380.5478[0.5255, 0.5682]0.9560
  • age_matched macro-F1 -0.0091 vs unrestricted; CIs overlap
  • sex_matched macro-F1 -0.0174 vs unrestricted; CIs overlap
  • multi_finding_removed macro-F1 +0.0002 vs unrestricted; CIs overlap

    • Image performance survives every control. Cataract-vs-rest AUROC stays near 0.94 under age matching and sex matching, and every confidence interval overlaps the unrestricted one. The demographic confound is real in the data but is not what the model is using.

    Method: matching is by downsampling within strata, so it closes the demographic route without reweighting or modelling.

    7. Deferral (RQ4, RQ5)

    The document never changes the predicted class. argmax(p_img) is the answer whenever the system answers; the document and its read-reliability only decide whether to answer.

    systemAURCerror-detection AUROCacc@90%acc@75%acc@50%
    image_confidence_only0.38890.58750.54320.54810.5889
    system_A_rules0.19730.88170.57410.65930.8667
    system_B_learned0.21070.86920.56790.64440.8889
    system_B_without_c_hat0.20320.87050.58020.6370.8667

    Lower AURC is better. system_B_without_c_hat isolates what the learned extraction-reliability estimate contributes - the one architectural claim this project makes.

    7b. Explainability (E12)

    Model: frozen ImageNet ResNet50 + linear head on cached embeddings. Head fitted on 4044 training-fold embeddings; attribution over held-out fold 0 - the head never saw these images.

    measurevalue
    FOV-mass ratio (observed)0.8364
    uniform-attribution baseline0.5348
    concentration ratio1.564x
    deletion AUC (mean)0.4687
    randomisation sanity checkPASS (r = -0.0943)

    Attribution concentrates inside the retinal field of view at 1.56x what uniform attribution would give, and the method passes the randomisation sanity check, so the maps do depend on the learned weights.

    What this permits us to say: attribution falls on retinal tissue rather than on borders or letterbox artefacts. What it does not permit: any claim that the model is looking at a lesion. There are no lesion masks and no ophthalmologist. The FOV-mass ratio answers a shortcut question, not a clinical one.

    Caveat: masking creates out-of-distribution inputs, so deletion AUC conflates attribution quality with behaviour on corrupted images. And not a fine-tuned diagnostic model; re-run after the Colab baselines.

    9. Statistical validation (E13)

    Seed stability. Every earlier result used split seed 42. The leakage comparison is re-run across [42, 7, 2024]; a finding that holds for only one random partition is not a finding.

    seedmodelimage-levelpatient-disjointinflationp
    42logistic0.55140.5476+0.00380.619208
    42knn_10.55850.5101+0.04840.0
    7logistic0.54500.5576-0.01260.036894
    7knn_10.55310.5091+0.04400.0
    2024logistic0.55000.5505-0.00050.840133
    2024knn_10.55890.5156+0.04340.0
    modelmean inflationsdminmax
    knn_1+0.04530.0027+0.0434+0.0484
    logistic-0.00310.0085-0.0126+0.0038

    Multiple comparisons. The project reports 13 paired tests. At alpha = 0.05 one spurious result in twenty is expected by construction, so Holm-Bonferroni is applied across the whole family. 5 of 13 survive correction:

  • leakage[knn_1,seed42] - p = 0.0 (threshold 0.003846)
  • leakage[knn_1,seed7] - p = 0.0 (threshold 0.004167)
  • leakage[knn_1,seed2024] - p = 0.0 (threshold 0.004545)
  • E1b[knn_1] - p = 0.0 (threshold 0.005)
  • E1b[knn_5] - p = 0.000646 (threshold 0.005556)

    • Holm rather than plain Bonferroni: uniformly more powerful at the same family-wise error rate, which matters when the smallest class has 182 patients.

    8. What is still outstanding

  • Fine-tuned baselines (E2/E3) need a GPU: colab/train_models.ipynb. Until they run, the protocol-ladder result is a lower bound.
  • XAI battery (E12) depends on a fine-tuned model to attribute over.
  • A real-document sanity check. No suitable public de-identified ophthalmic referral corpus was found; the search is recorded, and the corpus remains synthetic.
    • Academic screening prototype. Not a medical device and not a diagnosis.

    A qualified clinician reviews every case and makes every decision. Trained on a public research dataset with 203 cataract and 182 glaucoma patients. Referral documents used in development were synthetic. No prospective clinical validation.
